back: Two d orbitals (dx²−y², dz²) raised, three (dxy, dxz, dyz) lowered, because the ligands lie on the axes.
Three orbitals raised and two lowered; ΔE smaller than in an octahedral complex of the same ion.
Ligands split the d orbitals; an electron absorbs visible light of energy ΔE = hf and is promoted; the complementary colour is seen.
Sc³⁺ and Ti⁴⁺ (3d⁰), Zn²⁺ and Cu⁺ (3d¹⁰): no d-d transition is possible.
Red-orange absorbed → blue seen; green absorbed → pink/red-purple seen; violet-blue absorbed → yellow seen.
A different ligand (or shape) gives a different ΔE, so a different frequency of light is absorbed.
[Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ pale blue; [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ deep blue; [CuCl₄]²⁻ yellow (yellow-green in mixtures).
Filter of the absorbed (complementary) colour; standards → calibration graph of absorbance against concentration; read off the unknown.
